questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests edge proxy TLS termination, simple per-tenant rate limiting, and Docker Compose orchestration across DCs. It stays beginner-friendly while touching operational concerns.

## Key Concepts
- TLS termination at the edge
- Nginx limit_req for per-tenant rates
- Tenant discovery via HTTP header
- Docker Compose skeleton for cross-DC deployments

## Code Example
```nginx
# nginx.conf
http {
  map $http_x_tenant $limit {
    default 1r/s;
    'tenantA' 5r/s;
    'tenantB' 2r/s;
  }
  limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=per_tenant:10m rate=$limit;
  server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    location /api { limit_req zone=per_tenant burst=10; proxy_pass http://api:8080; }
  }
}
```

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml skeleton
version: 3.8
services:
  nginx:
    image: nginx:latest
    ports: ["443:443"]
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
      - ./certs:/etc/ssl/certs:ro
  api:
    image: your-api
  loader:
    image: alpine:latest
    command: sh -c 'cp /config/tenant_limits.json /nginx/tenant_limits.json'
    volumes:
      - ./config/tenant_limits.json:/config/tenant_limits.json:ro
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate 429 responses per tenant in tests?
- How would you handle a tenant with burst needs without impacting others?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests the ability to design tenant-aware observability with zero-downtime policy updates in a multi-DC docker-dca setup. It exercises integration of Traefik, OTel, and Docker Configs, plus handling of per-tenant behavior at the edge.

## Key Concepts

- OpenTelemetry collector as sidecar per service
- Docker Config for per-tenant policy (otel-policy)
- Traefik edge routing based on X-Tenant with tenant-scoped tagging
- Per-tenant sampling rates and log levels
- Dynamic policy updates without service restarts

## Code Example

```yaml
# docker-compose.yaml (minimal sketch)
version: '3.8'
services:
  api:
    image: myorg/api:latest
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    environment:
      - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4317
    configs:
      - source: otel-policy
        target: /etc/otel/policy.yaml
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector:latest
    command: ["--config=/otel-config/config.yaml"]
    volumes:
      - otel-config:/otel-config
configs:
  otel-policy:
    file: otel-policy.yaml
```

```yaml
# otel-policy.yaml (example)
tenants:
  tenantA:
    sample_rate: 0.2
    log_level: debug
  tenantB:
    sample_rate: 0.05
    log_level: info
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you version and rollback otel-policy changes?
- How would you handle aTenant that migrates DC mid-deployment without losing traces?

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example

```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  traefik:
    image: traefik:v2.10
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    command: |
      --providers.docker
      --entrypoints.web.address=:80
      --entrypoints.websecure.address=:443
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement traffic mirroring for safe shadow testing, validate latency impact, and design robust rollback.

## Key Concepts
- traffic mirroring with Nginx
- docker secrets/configs
- overlay networking in Swarm
- health checks and rollback policies
- non-disruptive canary/shadow deployments

## Code Example
```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  live-api:
    image: myorg/live
    secrets: [ tls_cert, tls_key ]
  shadow-api:
    image: myorg/shadow
    secrets: [ tls_cert, tls_key ]
  edge-nginx:
    image: nginx:latest
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
    depends_on: [live-api, shadow-api]
    configs: [ api-endpoints_config ]
configs:
  api-endpoints_config:
    external: true
secrets:
  tls_cert:
    external: true
  tls_key:
    external: true
networks:
  proxy:
    driver: overlay
    attachable: true
```

```nginx
# nginx.conf (simplified)
server {
  listen 443 ssl;
  ssl_certificate /run/secrets/tls_cert;
  ssl_certificate_key /run/secrets/tls_key;
  location / {
    proxy_pass http://live-api:8080;
    mirror /mirror_shadow;
  }
  location = /mirror_shadow {
    proxy_pass http://shadow-api:8081$request_uri;
    internal;
  }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you calculate and enforce a 95th percentile SLA during shadow testing?
- How would you automate rollback if shadow latency exceeds threshold for three consecutive minutes?

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests the ability to design end-to-end observability in a multi-DC, TLS-protected microservice environment. It validates understanding of cross-DC trace propagation, per-tenant context isolation, centralized collection, and sampling strategies.

## Key Concepts

- TLS termination at Traefik edge proxy

## Bootstrap Commands

```bash
# Generate TLS certificates
openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 \\
  -keyout traefik/tls.key -out traefik/tls.crt \\
  -subj "/CN=api.example.com"

# Start the stack
docker-compose up -d
```

## Minimal docker-compose.yml Skeleton

```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  traefik:
    image: traefik:v3.0
    command:
      - --api.insecure=true
      - --providers.docker
      - --entrypoints.web.address=":443"
      - --entrypoints.web.tls
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - ./traefik/tls.crt:/tls.crt
      - ./traefik/tls.key:/tls.key
    labels:
      - traefik.tls.creds=true

  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.110.0
    command: ["--config=/etc/otel-collector-config.yaml"]
    volumes:
      - ./otel-collector-config.yaml:/etc/otel-collector-config.yaml:ro
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # OTLP gRPC
      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP
      - "16686:16686" # Jaeger UI

  api-service:
    build: ./api
    environment:
      - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4317
      - OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=api-service
      - OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext,b3
    labels:
      - traefik.enable=true
      - traefik.http.routers.api.tls=creds
      - traefik.http.routers.api.rule=Host(`api.example.com`)

networks:
  default:
    name: dca-network
```

```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4317
      http:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318

processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 10s

  probabilistic:
    sampling_percentage: 10

  filter:
    spans:
      exclude:
        match_type: strict
        attributes:
          - key: tenant.id
            value: "low-priority"

exporters:
  otlp/tempo:

    endpoint: jaeger:14250
    tls:
      insecure: false

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      - receivers: [otlp]
      - processors: [batch, probabilistic, filter]
      - exporters: [otlp/tempo, jaeger]
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical mTLS implementation, Docker secrets management, and edge proxy configuration in a Swarm environment. Evaluates operational skills for secure service-to-service communication.

## Key Concepts
- Docker secrets for TLS certificate management
- Nginx mutual TLS verification and client certificate validation
- Client identity propagation to backend services via HTTP headers

## Code Example
```yaml
# skeleton docker-compose.yml
version: '3.9'
services:
  edge:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - '443:443'
    secrets:
      - source: nginx_server_cert
        target: server.crt
      - source: nginx_server_key
        target: server.key
      - source: nginx_ca_cert
        target: ca.pem
    configs:
      - source: nginx_config
        target: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
  api:
    image: your-api:latest
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
secrets:
  nginx_server_cert:
    external: true
  nginx_server_key:
    external: true
  nginx_ca_cert:
    external: true
configs:
  nginx_config:
    external: true
```

## Certificate Generation
```bash
# Create private CA
openssl genrsa -out ca.key 4096
openssl req -new -x509 -days 365 -key ca.key -out ca.pem

# Generate server certificate
openssl genrsa -out server.key 2048
openssl req -new -key server.key -out server.csr
openssl x509 -req -in server.csr -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial -out server.crt -days 365

# Generate client certificate
openssl genrsa -out client.key 2048
openssl req -new -key client.key -out client.csr
openssl x509 -req -in client.csr -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial -out client.crt -days 365

# Create Docker secrets
docker secret create nginx_server_cert server.crt
docker secret create nginx_server_key server.key
docker secret create nginx_ca_cert ca.pem
```

## Testing Commands
```bash
# Test with client certificate
curl --cert client.crt --key client.key --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api

# Test without client certificate (should fail)
curl --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api

# Verify client identity header
curl --cert client.crt --key client.key --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api -v | grep X-Client-Subject
```
